messages:
Ashley: ping team — Acme POC hit a cluster of 429s during a multi-part file upload test. Started ~35s into the run. Redacted log: https://acme-demo.logs/uploads (token removed)

AcmeOps: sample error we see: "{"error":"Too many requests","status":429}"
Response headers: x-ratelimit-limit: 100, x-ratelimit-remaining: 0, x-ratelimit-reset: 8, x-burst-remaining: 0

Samir: thanks. Important to know if this is per-route request cap or token-rate. How many parallel workers and average tokens per request?

Ashley: they ran 12 parallel workers, each uploading a 1.2MB payload that maps to ~1400 tokens, each worker doing ~0.9 requests/s for ~70s. Sales asking if we can safely bump quotas while the deal closes.

Miguel (oncall): rough math: 12 * 0.9 r/s = ~10.8 r/s -> ~648 r/min. Default per-route short-window is 100 rpm here, so per-route will be hit first. Token-rate: 10.8 r/s * 1400 tokens ~ 15120 tokens/s -> ~907k tokens/min, which would also exceed typical token-rate caps. Need to check org limits.

rate-limiter-bot: Quota snapshot for org "acme-corp": monthly_token_budget=10,000,000; tokens_used_mtd=2,140,201; per_minute_token_rate_limit=50000; per_route_requests_per_minute(/v1/upload): 100.

Jia: both limits will trip: per-route at ~100 rpm and token-rate at 50k tokens/min. Sales proposal: temporary bump to /v1/upload -> 700 rpm and token-rate 1,000,000 tokens/min for a 24-hour window, with auto-expiry. They want audit entries.

Samir: cautious — 1M tokens/min is high but for a short trial ok if we gate it to 24h and monitor. I'll apply a scoped policy with explicit TTL and create an audit note. Running CLI:
```
redwoodctl quotas update --org acme-corp --route /v1/upload --rpm 700 --token-rate 1000000 --ttl 24h --note "24h trial bump for Acme file-upload POC"
```

Samir: applied. change q-105731. Propagating (~5s).

rate-limiter-bot: Policy apply succeeded for org "acme-corp" (change q-105731). New per-route rpm: 700. New token_rate_limit: 1000000 tokens/min. TTL: 24h.

AcmeOps: re-ran upload; initial run still shows a few 429s at the start: [2026-07-12T14:03:21Z] POST /v1/upload 429 x-ratelimit-remaining:0 then mostly 200s after a few seconds.

Miguel: startup 429s likely due to window-edge propagation and burst exhaustion. Recommend enabling a burst_capacity to absorb the initial fan-out and a short ramp policy. Suggest burst_capacity=2500 over 60s and adding a small client-side token bucket to spread retries.

Samir: patching burst capacity:
```
redwoodctl quotas patch --org acme-corp --route /v1/upload --burst_capacity 2500 --burst_window 60 --note "smooth startup for Acme POC"
```
Samir: applied. change q-105732.

rate-limiter-bot: Burst policy updated for org "acme-corp" (change q-105732). burst_capacity: 2500, burst_window: 60s.

AcmeOps: reran. "Errors dropped from ~12% -> <0.5%. Upload finished." Thanks!

Jia: filing INF-4910: add a sales playbook for large file/import POCs (template: suggested rpm ranges, token-rate guidance, burst defaults, TTL requirements, monitoring checklist, and required audit fields).

Miguel: SRE note: for high-concurrency uploads recommend starting values: rpm=500-1000 for /v1/upload, token-rate=200k-2M tokens/min depending on payload, burst_capacity proportional to expected parallelism (e.g., 200 * parallel_workers), and always use client-side smoothing and jittered exponential backoff. Add a monitoring hook to auto-alert on >2% 1-min error rate after change.

Samir: audit: q-105731 and q-105732 recorded; both have TTL/auto-expiry. I added the sales note and linked INF-4910.

Ashley: will ask sales whether they need an extension beyond 24h. Marking the POC stage as mitigated. Appreciate the quick turn.

rate-limiter-bot: Monitoring: org "acme-corp" 1-min error rate decreased from 11.8% -> 0.4% after policy changes.
